name: Risen Biscuit
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ¾ cup lard or butter (half-and-half is a good rule)
ingredients.originalText: ¾ cup lard or butter (half-and-half is a good rule)

ingredients.name: flour to make a soft dough
ingredients.originalText: flour to make a soft dough

instructions.text: Mix over night, warming the milk slightly and melting the lard or butter
In the morning, roll out into a sheet three-quarters of an inch in thickness
Cut into round cakes and set these closely together in a pan
Let them rise for twenty minutes and bake twenty minutes
Alternatively, set the ingredients with half as much flour in the form of a thin sponge and work in the rest of the flour five hours later
Let this rise five hours more and proceed as already directed

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Mix over night, warming the milk slightly and melting the lard or butter
2. In the morning, roll out into a sheet three-quarters of an inch in thickness
3. Cut into round cakes and set these closely together in a pan
4. Let them rise for twenty minutes and bake twenty minutes
5. Alternatively, set the ingredients with half as much flour in the form of a thin sponge and work in the rest of the flour five hours later
6. Let this rise five hours more and proceed as already directed
